rationale: T requires evaluating whether required braking is omitted, so both the circumstances demanding braking and the corresponding braking behavior must be characterized. H-1 establishes the collision-threatening situation, while SG-1 and FR-7 establish braking performance itself as part of the evaluation, rather than merely a mechanism affecting it. P and its declared scope remain focused on that relationship without incorporating internal sensing, computation, communication, or failure-handling mechanisms.
determining_elements: “Operational situations where braking is required” identifies the conditions against which omission must be evaluated.
“Vehicle/system behavior” includes the braking response whose occurrence or omission is directly relevant to SG-1 and FR-7.
“Avoid collision with a road user or static obstacle” matches the hazardous outcome identified in H-1.

The scope’s “decide and execute braking” concerns the required functional response; it does not specify internal decision algorithms, control mechanisms, or additional mechanism-level timing behavior.
